what_it_does: Sparse matrix multiplication (SpGEMM—multiplying two matrices where most values are zero) is a bottleneck in many AI and scientific computing workloads. On GPUs, hash-based algorithms accumulate intermediate results efficiently, but they struggle with a trade-off: reducing hash collisions (when two entries hash to the same location) requires larger hash tables, which don't fit in the fast on-chip shared memory; fitting data into shared memory forces smaller tables with more collisions. This paper redesigns the accumulator data structure to pack more useful data into shared memory while minimizing hash collisions simultaneously. The approach rethinks how intermediate products are stored and merged, and is validated on three modern GPU architectures (Ampere, Ada Lovelace, Turing).
